action: No action needed; for awareness. The City of South Portland says service this week may be slower than usual and that some online portals, GIS mapping, Library Wi-Fi and meeting livestreams remain unavailable.
date_note: The city's notices say the IT team found the issue around 11:30 PM on Saturday, 14 November 2026 and shut the network down; this event is recorded on 22 November from the city's reopening notice of that day.
exec: A city network outage blamed on cybercriminal activity closed municipal buildings for a week; the city says some data was impacted and the investigation continues.
plain: A cybersecurity incident took down the City of South Portland's network, closing City Hall, Assessing and the Library. The city says buildings reopen on 23 November, some services are still down, and the investigation continues.

sources.name: City of South Portland: All City Buildings Open Monday, November 23, 2026

summary: The City of South Portland, Maine, says a cybersecurity incident caused a network IT outage that closed City Hall, Assessing and the Library; per the Press Herald, officials discovered it on 14 November and a preliminary investigation pointed to cybercriminal activity. The city says some data was impacted but most was not affected or accessed. Buildings reopen 23 November; the investigation is ongoing with no timeline.
title: South Portland, Maine: cybersecurity incident closed city buildings for a week; reopening 23 November

validation.note: The city's own notice (primary, southportland.gov) and the Portland Press Herald's report, which cites the city's releases. No attacker or ransomware named in either.
